title: Wind Power
objective: After this level you can explain how wind turbines work and where they work best.
summary: Wind turns blades and a rotor that drives a generator. Wind power rises with the cube of wind speed, so turbines go on windy plains, hilltops and water, on tall towers.

cards.headline: Double the wind speed, and you get eight times the power.
cards.body: That one rule explains where wind turbines stand and why they're so tall. First, what's going on up there when the blades turn?

cards.headline: A generator with wings
cards.body: A wind turbine's blades work like an airplane wing: moving air pushes them around. They turn a rotor, which drives a generator, either directly or through a shaft and gearbox. It all sits in a housing called the nacelle, on top of a tall tower. It's Level 8's generator again, except the wind does the spinning that steam does in Level 12's power plants.

cards.fact: The power in the wind grows with the cube of its speed.
cards.context: Double the speed and the power goes up two times two times two: eight times. That's why a site that's only a little windier can make far more electricity, and why small changes in wind speed swing a turbine's output so much.

cards.headline: Where the wind is worth it
cards.body: Good sites for big turbines average at least 13 mph of wind: smooth rounded hilltops, open plains, open water and mountain gaps that funnel the wind. Wind is also generally faster higher up, which is why the towers are so tall. In 2025, Texas, Iowa, Oklahoma, Kansas and Illinois made about 52% of US wind power. Across the country, wind made about a tenth of all electricity.

cards.headline: Wind: harnessed
learned: Blades turn a rotor that drives a generator in the nacelle
Wind power grows with the cube of wind speed
Best sites: plains, hilltops, open water, mountain gaps

questions.prompt: Inside a wind turbine, what do the turning blades ultimately drive?

options.label: A battery inside the tower
options.rationale: The blades drive a generator, not a battery.

options.label: A fan that pushes the air back
options.rationale: The turbine takes energy from the wind; it doesn't blow it.

questions.explanation: The blades turn a rotor that drives a generator, directly or through a gearbox, in the nacelle.

questions.prompt: One site's winds blow twice as fast as another's. How much more power does its wind carry?

options.label: Twice as much
options.rationale: Power grows faster than the speed.

options.label: Four times as much
options.rationale: That's the square; power follows the cube.

questions.explanation: Wind power follows the cube of the speed: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.

questions.prompt: Level 8 said something has to spin a generator's rotor. In a wind turbine, what does it?

options.label: Moving air pushing on the blades
Sunlight warming the tower
options.rationale: Sunlight isn't what turns the blades.

questions.explanation: The wind pushes the blades, which turn the rotor and the generator: Level 8's machine, spun by moving air.
